title: Signal-to-Commit roadmap: binding OKRs and cadence for hosted API + model catalog
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Create a repeatable 'Signal-to-Commit' playbook that translates product signals (usage growth, feature telemetry, CS feedback) into binding quarterly commitments for hosted API endpoints and model catalog onboarding. Scope: define decision gates, capacity hedges, canary windows, OKR linkage and rollback criteria for model swaps. This ticket produces a three-part deliverable: 1) an operational cadence document that product, eng, and infra agree to; 2) sprint-level sprint-grid templates that map signals -> funding/slots; 3) a lightweight dashboard spec capturing the 3 signals we will use during Q4 readiness (latency sprint risk, eval-regression delta, demand surge forecast). Trade-offs considered: stricter binding increases predictability but reduces flexibility to respond to model breakthroughs; the playbook prioritizes customer-facing stability for Q4 while preserving a small 10% experimental slot for emergent model upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Final cadence doc published in Confluence with sign-off from Eng, SRE, and Legal
Sprint-grid templates created for two cohorts (growth and enterprise) and stored in product drive
Dashboard prototype surfaced in Console for forecasting demand and model health; includes at least three signal widgets
A/B rollback and canary schedule templates included and validated by DevOps in a dry-run
OKR mappings: each named endpoint has a linked OKR and target metric defined for the quarter

notes: Decisions: adopt a two-lane commit model (Core endpoints with strict freeze + Growth endpoints with flexible swap slots). Reserve 10% capacity for experimental upgrades. Next steps: iterate dashboard prototype with Eng telemetry team (sprint 41), run one canary dry-run against staging before Q4 planning meeting. Document to be handed off to Program Management for scheduling.
